item: a Stop cuts a mailbox pull whose TCP connect has stalled, at once
summary: R647 registered a mailbox pull's socket for the Stop only once its TCP connect returned, so a server that never answered the connect held the pull until the 60 s timeout after a Stop. The socket is now created, registered and only then connected (_connect_registered, one candidate address at a time as socket.create_connection does), with the switch read every 0.1 s while the connect is in progress; on Linux the Stop's shutdown also aborts the connect itself. A refused or failed candidate is closed and leaves the Stop's list. The name lookup before the connect still cannot be interrupted. POP3's constructor now catches the Stop by its type, as IMAP's does. Release line: pressing Stop now also ends a newsletter mailbox pull that is still waiting for the mail server to accept the connection.
